---
title: "Query-Key-Value (QKV)"
description: "The three learned representations used by attention to compute relevance weights and combine information."
term: "Query-Key-Value (QKV)"
letter: "Q"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Attention uses three roles: a **query** says what a position is looking for,
**keys** describe what each position offers, and **values** carry the
information to combine. Matching queries with keys determines how much of
each value contributes.

## Technical explanation

Given input representations $X$, learned matrices produce
$Q=XW_Q$, $K=XW_K$, and $V=XW_V$. Scaled dot-product attention is
$\mathrm{softmax}(QK^\mathsf{T}/\sqrt{d_k})V$. Multi-head attention applies
separate projections in parallel and combines the resulting representations.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

QKV is the core computation behind Transformer attention. Its tensor shapes,
memory use, and sequence-length scaling influence model implementation,
training efficiency, and inference latency.

## How it works

Each query is compared with keys to produce attention scores. Softmax
converts each score row into weights, and those weights form a weighted sum
of values. In self-attention all three projections come from the same
sequence; cross-attention can source keys and values from another sequence.

## Practical example

In language-model self-attention, every token position generates a query,
key, and value. A token can then combine information from earlier positions,
subject to the model's causal mask.

## Common misconceptions

- “Key” and “value” are learned vector roles, not necessarily stored
  database keys and literal text values.
- Query, key, and value are not three separate models; they are usually
  projections within one attention layer.
